messages.author: 744ad518e240c51e
messages.subject: Model Equivalence, factor mean invariance
parts:
Hi all,


I am trying to investigate measurement invariance across two groups. Here is my model (with 9 indicators and 2 factors):

model <- '

general =~ Task9 + Task7 + Task3 + Task1 + Task4 + Task6

shifting =~ Task2 + Task5 + Task8

Task2~~Task7'

 

I have already established configural, metric and scale invariance. In the next step, I want to test whether factor means are invariant:

 

invar8 <- cfa(model,data = EF.data, group = "Group",group.equal = c("loadings","intercepts","residuals","means")

 

After constraining factor means to be equal, the model gets significantly worse. Since I have two latent factors (General and Shifting), I tried to free one factor mean at a time, to see which factor mean is causing the failure of establishing a factor mean invariance. So I did the following:

 

invar8a <- cfa(model,data = EF.data, group = "Group",group.equal = c("loadings","intercepts","residuals","means"), group.partial = c("shifting~1"))

 

However, this does not seem to work. When I look at fit measures, the degree of freedom is the same as when no factor mean is freed. I don’t understand this (shouldn’t it be 1 df less, as we have one more factor mean to estimate).

 

So I used an alternative way to test the same idea.

model.mean1 <-'

general =~ Task9 + Task7 + Task3 + Task1 + Task4 + Task6

shifting =~ Task2 + Task5 + Task8

Task2~~Task7

general ~ c(0,0)*1

shifting ~ c(0,NA)*1'

 

invar9a <- cfa(model.mean1,data = EF.data, group = "Group",group.equal = c("loadings","intercepts","residuals")


So here is my question:

1) Is this the correct way to proceed when failing to establish factor mean invariance?

2) Why fit invar8a does not work? Are models 8a and 9a equivalent?


Many thanks in advance if you have any ideas/comments on this.

Regards,

Beinan

messages.subject: Re: Model Equivalence, factor mean invariance
parts:
On 06/10/2015 09:11 PM, Beinan Zhou wrote:
> *invar8a <- cfa(model,data = EF.data, group = "Group",group.equal =

> c("shifting~1"))*

Nope. This will not work because (unlike factor loadings and
intercepts), the means are already fixed to zero by default, and are
only freed for the second group if they become identified.

> So I used an alternative way to test the same idea.
>

> *model.mean1 <-'*
>
> *general =~ Task9 + Task7 + Task3 + Task1 + Task4 + Task6*
>
> *shifting =~ Task2 + Task5 + Task8*
>
> *Task2~~Task7*
>
> *general ~ c(0,0)*1 *
>
> *shifting ~ c(0,NA)*1'*
>
> **
>
> *invar9a <- cfa(model.mean1,data = EF.data, group = "Group",group.equal
> = c("loadings","intercepts","residuals")*

Yes, this is the way. In fact, you do not need th 'shifting' line.

Yves.
